prompt_md: A tack lands point-up with an unknown chance; beforehand, every value from 0% to 100% is equally likely. It lands point-up 3 times in a row. Chance the next one does?
prompt_short: Unknown bias, uniform prior. Three point-ups in a row. Chance of a fourth?
hint_md: Let the three results update your belief about the tack.
explain_intuition_md: Three ups in a row is evidence that this tack favors landing up, so your estimate should rise. Averaging over every possible bias, weighted by how well it explains three ups, gives 4 in 5. Treating the tosses as unrelated coin flips gives 50%, but the shared unknown bias links them.
explain_math_md: With a uniform prior on $p$: $$P(\text{up} \mid 3 \text{ ups}) = \frac{\int_0^1 p^4 \, dp}{\int_0^1 p^3 \, dp} = \frac{1/5}{1/4} = \tfrac45$$
